phrase: Insanity is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting different results
finding: Prominent misattribution to Einstein; popularization via 1980s recovery-community and fiction use is stronger than any Einstein coinage claim, while named authorship remains incomplete.
searchScope: Quote Investigator dossier, Snopes summary, and cited 1981 newspaper / 1983 novel trail. Did not re-inspect Knoxville News-Sentinel microfilm beyond QI.
evidenceReviewed: QI (2017) on early-1980s recovery-community trail and Rita Mae Brown 1983; Ultimate Quotable Einstein misattribution listing via QI.

assertions.subject: Albert Einstein
assertions.publicStatement: Current evidence does not securely support coinage by Albert Einstein; major Einstein quotation references list the line as misattributed.

assertions.subject: Rita Mae Brown, Sudden Death (1983) and later Einstein myth
assertions.publicStatement: Popularized in mainstream fiction by Rita Mae Brown’s 1983 novel Sudden Death, then later by unsupported Einstein attributions from around 1990.

assertions.subject: Early-1980s recovery-community print trail
assertions.publicStatement: Attribution investigations place early documented use in early-1980s recovery-community print; the earliest newspaper hardcopy was not independently re-inspected in this corpus.

assertions.subject: Named author and earliest hardcopy in this corpus
assertions.publicStatement: The record remains incomplete as to a named original author, and the earliest newspaper trail (early 1980s recovery-community print) was not independently re-inspected as primary hardcopy in this corpus.

sources.title: Insanity Is Doing the Same Thing Over and Over Again and Expecting Different Results
sources.author: Garson O’Toole
sources.shortExcerpt: There is no substantive evidence that Einstein wrote or spoke the statement above. … based on current evidence the saying originated in one of the twelve-step communities.
